name: Help Scout

field_reviews.reason: Live developer.helpscout.com authentication page: Inbox API 2.0 is OAuth 2.0 with Authorization Code (redirection-based, for integrations used by other Help Scout users) and Client Credentials flows.
Inbox API confirms both OAuth2 flows; the separate Docs API uses an API key sent as the Basic auth username, matching the draft's api_key/basic_auth entries.

Help Scout is a paid product with self-serve trial signup; OAuth2 apps are created self-serve under Your Profile > My Apps in any account, and API access is included in Standard/Plus/Pro plans per the vendor's MCP support article.
Inbox API 2.0 covers conversations, customers, mailboxes, users, reports, webhooks; Docs API covers the knowledge base.

Help Scout now also operates a hosted MCP endpoint (https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp), generally available; per the batch's own convention (Podio/Pylon/Slack drafts list mcp when an official server exists) the protocols list should include mcp.

The draft's 'none_found' for a vendor MCP is wrong: Help Scout's own blog announced its MCP server is out of beta and generally available, hosted at https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp (read-only, per-user OAuth, Standard/Plus/Pro plans). The draft missed it because it is documented in the help center (docs.helpscout.com), not the developer portal it searched. Composio HELP_SCOUT toolkit (129 tools, OAuth2) and the drewburchfield community server both re-confirmed.
Self-serve trial signup plus self-serve OAuth2 app creation; API fully documented and open.
No gate beyond being a (trialable) paid product; no partner approval required for API access.

notes: Auth, access, breadth and Composio toolkit (129 tools, OAuth2) all re-verified live. Major correction: Help Scout ships an official vendor MCP server, GA at mcp.helpscout.net/mcp (vendor blog + help-center article updated Aug 6, 2026; read-only, per-user credentials, plans with API access). Corrected mcp_status (removed none_found, added official_vendor_mcp) and api_protocols (added mcp). The vendor documents MCP only in its help center, not on developer.helpscout.com, which is why the draft's developer-portal search found nothing.
